<compartment start="155" end="201" title="Chorus: op-log-as-source-of-truth architecture established" episode_type="design,infra" importance="95">
<p1>
Major architecture session for the Chorus CRDT sync engine. Initial implementation stored materialized document state as the source of truth; the op log was an audit trail appended after each mutation. Under concurrent editing from 3+ clients, three-way merge conflicts produced divergent materialized states that couldn't be reconciled without replaying the log anyway — the materialized state was losing the information needed for conflict resolution.

U: "every time we have a 3-way merge we end up replaying the log to fix it anyway, maybe the log should just BE the truth"

Pivoted to op-log-as-source-of-truth: a document is defined by its full sequence of operations in causal order. Materialized snapshots are derived on-read, cached in SnapshotCache (backed by Redis, keyed by document_id + vector_clock_hash), and invalidated synchronously when new ops arrive. Synchronous invalidation is critical — an earlier async prototype let fast-editing clients read stale snapshots for up to 200 ms, which caused visible cursor jumps in the collaboration UI.

U: "how large does the log get before we need to compact"

Compaction triggers at max_ops_before_compact=10000 per document. Below that threshold, full replay from the earliest checkpoint is fast enough (<50 ms in benchmarks). Above it, a compaction job creates a new checkpoint snapshot and tombstones older ops. Vector clocks used for causal ordering across clients, not wall clock.

U: "ok, let's commit to this model"

Decision documented in docs/arch/op-log.md. Core implementation in crates/chorus-core/src/log.rs and crates/chorus-core/src/snapshot.rs. Commit 7e3d4c2.
</p1>
<p2>
Chorus uses op-log-as-source-of-truth: document is its causal op sequence (vector clocks). Snapshots derived on-read, cached in SnapshotCache (Redis, document_id + vector_clock_hash), invalidated synchronously on new op arrival — async caused stale reads under concurrent edit load. Compaction at max_ops_before_compact=10000. U: "every time we have a 3-way merge we end up replaying the log to fix it anyway" — this was the pivot signal. docs/arch/op-log.md.
</p2>
<p3>
Chorus op log is the source of truth; snapshots derived on-read and cached; compaction at 10 k ops/document; synchronous cache invalidation required.
</p3>
<p4>
OpLog; SnapshotCache; vector_clock; max_ops_before_compact=10000; crates/chorus-core; synchronous invalidation
</p4>
</compartment>
<facts>
<ARCHITECTURE>
* Chorus document state is defined by the op log in causal order (vector clocks); materialized snapshots are derived-on-read cache entries, not the source of truth.
</ARCHITECTURE>
<CONSTRAINTS>
* Chorus SnapshotCache invalidation must be synchronous on new op arrival; async invalidation causes stale reads visible to concurrent editing clients (observed: up to 200 ms staleness in async prototype).
</CONSTRAINTS>
<PROJECT_RULES>
* Never mutate a Chorus materialized snapshot directly; always append an op to the log and re-derive the snapshot.
</PROJECT_RULES>
<NAMING>
* Chorus core types: OpLog (crates/chorus-core/src/log.rs), SnapshotCache (crates/chorus-core/src/snapshot.rs).
</NAMING>
<CONFIG_VALUES>
* Chorus compaction threshold: max_ops_before_compact=10000 per document.
</CONFIG_VALUES>
</facts>

<trajectory_correction at_compartment="7">

  <after_strategy>Op log is authoritative and defines the document; materialized snapshots derived on-read from log, cached in SnapshotCache with synchronous invalidation</after_strategy>

</trajectory_correction>

<compartment start="361" end="392" title="Tethys: JWT refresh not re-fetching tenant roles after role change" episode_type="investigation,bug,refactor" importance="78">
<p1>
Bug report: a user whose tenant admin role was revoked could still access admin-only endpoints for up to 15 minutes after revocation. Investigation showed JWT access tokens carry tenant_roles claim at issue time; revoking a role in the DB doesn't invalidate existing tokens, which remain valid until TTL expiry.

U: "this is a security issue, not a UX issue — we need role changes to propagate faster than 15 minutes"

The clean fix was the refresh path: on token refresh, re-query tenant membership and embed fresh claims. But the refresh endpoint (auth/token/refresh.go) was only re-issuing basic claims (sub, iat, exp) and copying TenantRoles verbatim from the incoming token. One-line omission: refreshedClaims.TenantRoles was never populated from a fresh DB lookup.

Fixed by pulling tenant membership at refresh time and embedding in the new token. Added an integration test: revoke a role, trigger a refresh, assert the refreshed token does not carry the revoked role.

U: "what's the max lag now"

Max lag is bounded by access_token_ttl=900 s for clients that never call refresh. Any client that refreshes (which the SDK does automatically on 401) gets updated claims immediately. Acceptable under current threat model. Committed 9d7ca2c.
</p1>
<p2>
Tethys JWT refresh was copying tenant_roles from old token instead of re-fetching; revoked roles persisted for up to access_token_ttl=900 s. Fixed in auth/token/refresh.go: fresh tenant membership fetched at refresh time (9d7ca2c). U: "this is a security issue" — treated as immediate priority. Max lag now bounded by TTL for clients that never refresh.
</p2>
<p3>
Tethys token refresh now embeds freshly-fetched tenant_roles; revoked role lag bounded by access_token_ttl=900 s.
</p3>
<p4>
JWT refresh; tenant_roles; access_token_ttl=900s; refresh_token_ttl=86400s; auth/token/refresh.go
</p4>
</compartment>
<facts>
<CONSTRAINTS>
* Tethys JWT access tokens carry tenant_roles at issue time; role changes do not invalidate existing tokens — a revoked role remains usable until token expiry (up to access_token_ttl=900 s for clients that don't refresh).
</CONSTRAINTS>
<PROJECT_RULES>
* Tethys token refresh must always re-fetch tenant_roles from the DB; never carry role claims forward from the incoming token.
</PROJECT_RULES>
<CONFIG_VALUES>
* Tethys token TTLs: access_token_ttl=900 s, refresh_token_ttl=86400 s.
</CONFIG_VALUES>
</facts>

<compartment start="142" end="170" title="b2d4a79 round-2 reviews: N1/N2/N3 + frozen-snapshot fixes → c051577" episode_type="bug,refactor" importance="80">
<p1>
With the B1/B2/B3 + I1/I2/I3 + S1 fixes committed as b2d4a79, I ran the round-2 verification. E2E round 2 at b2d4a79 came back PASS on chain a–i plus six round-2 additions (brief `metrics` key ABSENT not null; text/plain metadata → 400; duplicate `front` → 400; cross-cycle `enrolled_reconciled`; archive exactly 2 distinct result rows/object keys with `content_hash`; cleanup of the occupied request; K untouched 0/NULL/0), tree clean at both ends.

Oracle R1 re-review (ora-5, `ses_f70d6639bffeJHH4g6Z16SyzsV`) at b2d4a79 returned FAIL: B1/B2/B3/I1/I2/I3 were all COMPLIANT, S1 was only a DEVIATION (text-param metadata Content-Type still unchecked; a file-form metadata part plus a text-param metadata part was not detected as duplicate), and it raised new findings — BLOCKER N1 (the result-image archive wrapped `storage.put()` inside the PG transaction, so a crash between put and commit left a sensitive result object with no T11 row, undiscoverable and uncleanable by `media.cleanup`), IMPORTANT N2 (`_mark_failed`/`_mark_plan_failed` committed terminal business state in their own transaction and then raised `JobFailed`, so T12 failed in a second transaction and a crash or lease expiry between them could leave T05/T06 failed while T12 was recovered and possibly ended succeeded), and SUGGESTION N3 (a stale fence produced two WARNs).

Oracle R2 first review (ora-6, `ses_f70b71d45ffeJs6PNR09qcW1iw`) at b2d4a79 also returned FAIL: BLOCKER — `_frozen_rules` validated only presence and three outer container types, so a snapshot missing `report`/`model`/provenance, or holding malformed nested ranges/regions/bounds, could still publish a ready plan or throw an unhandled exception instead of terminating `PLAN_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`; SUGGESTION — the D.md handoff was stale.

U: 总协调针对最新Oracle N2明确裁定（一次增量授权）：D为本次唯一公共complete_failure及必要调用接入/测试负责人。最小允许business callback与T12失败/重试状态在同一短事务提交；遵循业务→任务锁顺序，检查owner/lease_revision、租约未过期及业务输入版本；旧/失效领取权不能写业务或任务。callback失败整体回滚，不把业务failed的任务记succeeded、不吞失败，事务/callback内禁止网络调用。明确可重试与终态业务映射，沿原attempt预算，不改变B通知失败行为；无callback调用方保持兼容。公共loop/启动/B周期调度不在此授权范围；必要调用接入不能借此扩大公共loop变更。N1按Oracle建议稳定pending先提交再锁外put；pending请求/对象标识必须可重试复用，并发接纳/清理安全，不凭超时删活跃引用。M4畸形冻结快照fail-closed并有稳定业务错误。

Two fix lanes ran concurrently. Java fix-5 closed the S1 residual: `AssessmentMultipartParser` replaced the file-absent-only duplicate check with `metadataParamCount` logic (>1 text params → 400; file-part metadata + 1 text param → 400; single text param accepted), with `multipartMetadataFormStrictness` added to `AssessmentAcceptanceIT`; 183/0/0.

Python fix-3 delivered N1/N2/R2/N3. N1 restored a two-phase archive in `dshared/dmedia.py`: tx1 under `pg_advisory_xact_lock('d:result-archive:'+aid+':'+pv)` loads-by-ref, reuses or inserts a pending row with `content_type`, and commits; then `storage.put(object_key, data)` runs outside any transaction with the same key on every retry; tx2 `_promote_tx` conditionally promotes `state='pending'`→`available` with a full recheck on rowcount 0. N2 added `complete_failure(business_tx=…)` — `JobFailed` gained a `business_tx` attribute, `runtime/loop.py` forwards it, and the callback runs inside the same `engine.begin()` before the guarded T12 update; `_REQUEUE`/`_MARK_FAILED` gained `AND lease_until >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; D's terminal writes became `_mark_failed_tx`/`_mark_plan_failed_tx` callbacks with entry convergence kept as defense-in-depth. R2 rewrote `_frozen_rules` to fully validate `schema_version`, report UUIDs/photo_version, model strings, capability provenance, finite ordered parameter ranges with units, unique bounded regions, and positive ordered N bounds, returning None → fenced `PLAN_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`. N3 demoted the handler-side `*.fenced_write_stale` logs to DEBUG. 158 passed (137 → +21). Shared-file scope: `runtime/complete.py`, `handlers/__init__.py`, `runtime/loop.py` (+42/−4). Committed as c051577 (17 files, +962/−182).
</p1>
<p2>
After b2d4a79, E2E round 2 passed; Oracle R1 re-review (ora-5) FAILed on N1 (result-image `storage.put` inside the PG transaction → an object can persist with no T11 row), N2 (`_mark_failed`/`_mark_plan_failed` commit terminal business state in a separate transaction from T12 failure), and N3 (double WARN), with S1 a DEVIATION; Oracle R2 first review (ora-6) FAILed on incomplete frozen-snapshot validation. 总协调 authorized D as sole owner of the public `complete_failure` business callback. Fixes: Java multipart metadata duplicate/Content-Type strictness (183 tests); Python two-phase archive, `complete_failure(business_tx=…)` with `JobFailed.business_tx` forwarded by the loop, full `_frozen_rules` snapshot validation → `PLAN_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`, and N3 log demotion (158 tests). Shared files: `runtime/complete.py`, `handlers/__init__.py`, `runtime/loop.py`. Committed as c051577.
</p2>
<p3>
Oracle R1/R2 found N1 (object storage cannot roll back with the PG transaction), N2 (terminal business write not atomic with T12 failure), and incomplete frozen-snapshot validation after b2d4a79. The fixes introduced the two-phase archive, the public `complete_failure(business_tx=…)` atomic-failure path, and full snapshot contract validation, committed as c051577.
</p3>
<p4>
c051577; N1 two-phase archive; complete_failure business_tx; PLAN_SNAPSHOT_INVALID
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="171" end="189" title="c051577 round-3: F1 digest-first archive fix → 4ac4835" episode_type="bug" importance="74">
<p1>
With c051577 committed I dispatched the third round: ora-5 R1 third review, ora-6 R2 re-review, and E2E round 3.

Oracle R1 third review at c051577 returned FAIL. N1/N2/N3/S1 were all COMPLIANT (closed), but it raised BLOCKER F1 — for the same `provider_ref`, a second image with different content (different MIME or bytes) reused the same T11 row and object key and overwrote the stored object while T11 kept the first image's `content_type`/`content_hash`/`byte_size`, so metadata and bytes diverged and the report could double-reference the same media ID — plus SUGGESTION F2 (`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is transaction-start time, so a lease guard evaluated after a long callback could still pass after actual expiry).

E2E round 3 at c051577 passed (chain a–i plus the full round-2 set and round-3 additions: metadata file+text param → 400, two text params → 400, single text param → 202, two-phase archive shape with 2 available rows / 0 pending). Oracle R2 re-review (ora-6) at c051577 returned PASS-with-notes with `blockingFindings` empty (snapshot blocker CLOSED, N2 COMPLIANT).

Python fix F1 rewrote `dshared/dmedia.py`: pre-validation now validates every image and computes `byte_size` + `content_hash=sha256(data)`, rejecting a duplicate `provider_ref` within one invocation as terminal `PROVIDER_CONTRACT_VIOLATION` before any DB/storage side effect; the pending INSERT persists `content_type`/`byte_size`/`content_hash` (the V1 CHECKs permit this on pending); `available` rows are reused only when content_type, byte_size and content_hash all match, and any mismatch is terminal with no put and no mutation; `pending` rows with a persisted hash must match. A session-scoped `pg_advisory_lock(hashtextextended('d:result-archive:'||aid||':'||pv,0))` was held across tx1→put→tx2 on a dedicated lock connection, released in `finally` (invalidate on unlock failure). `assessment_analyze.py` was untouched (its `except ArchiveError` already routes `exc.code` to the fenced terminal path). Added three F1 tests plus zero-provider-invocation assertions; 161 passed. Committed as 4ac4835 (3 files, +304/−98).
</p1>
<p2>
With c051577 committed, E2E round 3 passed and Oracle R2 re-review returned PASS-with-notes (`blockingFindings` empty). Oracle R1 third review FAILed on F1: the same `provider_ref` with different content reused the same T11 row/object key and overwrote the stored object while T11 kept the old MIME/hash/size. The fix rewrote `dmedia.py` to validate and sha256 every image up front, reject duplicate refs and divergent content before any put, and persist expected MIME/size/hash on the pending row; a session-scoped advisory lock across tx1→put→tx2 serialized archive per task+version. 161 tests. Committed as 4ac4835.
</p2>
<p3>
Oracle R1 third review found that same-`provider_ref` different content could overwrite a stored result object while T11 kept the old metadata. The fix made the archive digest-first (validate + sha256 before any side effect; reject divergent content before put). Committed as 4ac4835.
</p3>
<p4>
4ac4835; F1 digest-first archive integrity; PROVIDER_CONTRACT_VIOLATION
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="190" end="224" title="4ac4835 round-4: G1 connection-pool starvation + F2 clock_timestamp → c5b78d8" episode_type="bug,refactor" importance="78">
<p1>
With 4ac4835 committed (F1 fix), I dispatched the fourth round: ora-5 R1 fourth review, ora-6 R2 bounded rebind, and E2E round 4.

Oracle R2 bounded rebind at 4ac4835 returned CONFIRMED PASS: the ten R2 production files were byte-identical, the delta was exactly `dmedia.py` + two test files (+304/−98), and the strengthened plan tests were accepted; it corrected my claim that `dmedia` is imported only by `assessment_analyze` (it is also imported by `identity_enroll`).

Oracle R1 fourth review at 4ac4835 returned FAIL. F1 was COMPLIANT (closed), but it raised BLOCKER G1 — the session advisory lock connection was held across the whole archive call while tx1 and tx2 each acquired another connection from the same bounded pool (default `pool_size=5`, `claim_batch=5`, `max_overflow=0`), so with five concurrent archives every thread held one connection and waited for a second, deadlocking the pool and starving the lease renewer and health queries.

E2E round 4 at 4ac4835 was STOPPED and invalidated: an external process modified the shared worktree mid-run (dirty=3 — `dmedia.py`, `.gitignore`, test file changed externally) and dropped `mvp_d_dev`, so the redone chain ran uncommitted code and could not be certified against the commit; final-SHA certification was withheld.

U: 总协调再次确认一次增量：授权D唯一负责runtime/loop.py except JobFailed→实际_finish_failure→complete_failure透传business_tx最小必要调用链；保留无callback行为、业务→任务锁顺序、失败重试预算，callback异常整事务回滚；不扩大启动/调度/B扫描。F2：有效租约使用真正当前时间，而不是事务起始CURRENT_TIMESTAMP；过期领取者不得提交业务结果，相关公共依赖扩围如需改动先报最小范围。F1：固定预期hash/size/MIME，同ref异内容在覆盖前拒绝，不先覆盖后校验。继续原任务与审查，不重派整任务/新会话；scheduled15不变。

Python fix G1 rewrote `dmedia.py` to a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock` inside tx1 and to hold at most one pool connection at any instant (tx1 → release → connection-less `storage.put` → tx2 → release), removing the session lock, the dedicated `lock_conn` and the `invalidate()` path; legacy `content_hash IS NULL` pending rows are claimed atomically inside tx1 via `UPDATE … WHERE id=:id AND content_hash IS NULL`; put-failure retains the pending row for retry. It added a small-pool starvation test (`pool_size=2`, two different assessments, both complete) and a legacy NULL-hash divergence test; 163 passed.

Python fix F2 then changed the lease predicates in `runtime/complete.py` (`_REQUEUE`, `_MARK_FAILED`, `_DEFER`) and `dshared/dfence.py` (`_FENCE`) from `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` to `clock_timestamp()`, so an expired claimer can never commit business results when a callback burns the lease mid-transaction, and added `tests/test_lease_clock.py`; 171 passed. Both fixes were then committed as c5b78d8.
</p1>
<p2>
With 4ac4835 committed, Oracle R2 bounded rebind returned CONFIRMED PASS (ten R2 production files byte-identical) and E2E round 4 was STOPPED/invalidated by external worktree interference (dirty tree, `mvp_d_dev` dropped), withholding final-SHA certification. Oracle R1 fourth review FAILed on G1: the session advisory lock held one pool connection across the whole archive while tx1 and tx2 each took another from the same bounded pool, so with `pool_size=claim_batch=5` five concurrent archives deadlocked the pool. 总协调 then authorized D as sole owner of the loop.py→`_finish_failure`→`complete_failure` passthrough and ruled F2 (use true wall-clock, not transaction-start `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`) and F1 (fix expected hash/size/MIME; reject divergent content before overwrite). The G1 fix moved to a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock` with at most one pool connection per call (tx1 → put without a connection → tx2), atomically claiming legacy NULL-hash pending rows; 163 tests. The F2 fix changed the lease predicates in `complete.py` and `dfence.py` to `clock_timestamp()`; 171 tests. Committed as c5b78d8.
</p2>
<p3>
Oracle R1 fourth review found G1 — the archive's session advisory lock starved the bounded connection pool under default concurrency. The fix switched to a transaction-scoped advisory lock holding at most one pool connection per call; F2 replaced `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` with `clock_timestamp()` in all lease guards so expired claimers cannot commit. Committed as c5b78d8.
</p3>
<p4>
G1 tx-scoped advisory lock; one-connection discipline; clock_timestamp lease guards; c5b78d8
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="225" end="248" title="c5b78d8 fifth round: R2 rebind #2 CONFIRMED + E2E r5 PASS + R1 fifth review + final authorization" episode_type="bug" importance="70">
<p1>
Committed the combined G1+F2 fixes as c5b78d8 (6 files, +511/−137: `.gitignore`, `dmedia.py`, `complete.py`, `dfence.py`, `test_lease_clock.py`, `test_result_archive_concurrency.py`).

Oracle R2 rebind #2 at c5b78d8 (ora-6) returned CONFIRMED PASS_WITH_WARNINGS: `complete.py` changed exactly the three predicates `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`→`clock_timestamp()` in `_REQUEUE`/`_MARK_FAILED`/`_DEFER`, `dfence.py` changed only `_FENCE.lease_live`, and the eight other R2 production files were byte-identical; it flagged an IMPORTANT test weakness — the mid-transaction timing tests slept before their first SQL statement, so with lazy transaction commencement they might also pass under the old `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` semantics — and recommended executing SQL before sleeping.
